title: cost: automation for batching/caching defaults, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost across common production workloads by automating conservative defaults for batching and KV/prefix caching, surfacing quantization profile suggestions per-model, and adding unit-economics tooling to the Console and CLI so SREs and platform engineers can validate cost/latency tradeoffs. This PR wires together three workstreams into one deployable feature set.

What this PR does:
- Add an AutoTune service that computes conservative batching and cache defaults based on request histograms and live latencies; stores suggestions in model metadata.
- Introduce model-level quantization profile recommendations (fp16/int8/llm-int8-like presets) and a mechanism to mark "verified" profiles after quick smoke runs.
- Surface unit-economics suggestions in Redwood Console (Cost -> Unit Economics) and expose a new CLI command `redwood unit-econ suggest` for offline evaluation.
- Add telemetry: new metrics (redwood.autotune.suggested_batch_size, redwood.unit_econ.estimated_token_cost_usd) and dashboards.
- Configs: new permissive defaults for hosted customers, opt-out flag for Dedicated/Private in config.
- Tests: unit and integration tests for autotune heuristics and quant profile matching plus an e2e canary job.

Checklist:
- [x] AutoTune service implementation + API
- [x] Quantization profile recommendation engine + quick smoke validation
- [x] Console UI components and API endpoints
- [x] CLI `unit-econ` subcommand
- [x] Telemetry and dashboards
- [x] Unit/integration tests and canary pipeline

Compatibility: defaults are conservative (small batch sizes, cache TTLs tuned to reduce tail latency impact). Dedicated/Private customers are opt-in for automated changes; managed-hosted accounts get suggestions applied by default but can disable via org settings.

Performance notes: in our internal canary across 12 production-like workloads we observed median token cost reduction of 12-18% with no regressions to p95 latency in 11/12 workloads; one heavy short-sequence workload showed a 6% p95 regression which is handled by the conservative fallback in the runtime (autotune will reduce batching for that route).

Relevant links: Linear ENG-4821 (autotune), ENG-4873 (unit-econ), design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/autotune-design, internal dashboard link (redwood-internal/dashboards/unit-econ).

Notes for reviewers: focus review on autotune heuristics and the API contract for suggestions (ModelSuggestion proto). The Console changes are mostly UI wiring; backend API must be stable.

feat(runtime): apply conservative batching/cache defaults from model metadata
feat(quant): quant profile recommendation engine + smoke runner
feat(console): unit-econ UI and backend endpoints
chore(tests): integration tests for autotune and unit-econ canary
ci: add canary pipeline that runs e2e cost regression suite
review_comments: Diego Marquez: Overall looks good. Two requests: please add a config flag to prevent AutoTune from changing batch sizes for routes with explicit per-route overrides, and add a short TTL for suggested profiles so we don't keep stale suggestions.
Aisha Patel: Thanks Diego - added route_override check and suggestion_ttl config (60m default). Updated tests to cover TTL behavior.
Emma Liu: Is there a risk of repeated quantization smoke runs causing GPU contention on small clusters? Suggest rate limiting the smoke_runner.
Aisha Patel: Good point - added a global rate limiter and exponential backoff for smoke runs in src/quant/smoke_runner.py. Also added a metric quant.smoke_runs.rate_limited.
Ravi Srinivasan: CI flake in integration test on first run; re-ran and green. Please ensure e2e canary is gated behind a feature flag in production rollout.
Aisha Patel: Canary runs are gated behind release flags; added FEATURE_UNIT_ECON_CANARY in helm values and documented in deploy notes.
release_notes: Add AutoTune service to compute conservative batching/caching defaults, quantization profile recommendations, and unit-economics tooling (Console + CLI). Default suggestions applied for hosted accounts; opt-out available. Adds telemetry and dashboards. Estimated 12-18% token cost reduction on canary workloads.
performance_summary: Canary across 12 workloads: median token cost reduction 12-18%, p95 latency regressions observed in 1/12 workloads (6%); runtime fallback prevented customer impact. Telemetry: redwood.autotune.suggested_batch_size and redwood.unit_econ.estimated_token_cost_usd added.
